intel.summary: Restored intel-core-fixes-001's snapshot (2309421), which changed nothing outside the owned paths. P1: step.ts replaces defer/flushPending with one sighting accumulator per player per step. The pending types (at a boundary), losses, journal replacements and targeted requests all add to it, and a new pass 4 makes one decision per player: uncapped, one message lists the types in type order with sectors drawn at send time, and requests are answered 'sighting'; capped, the free types become the one pending set and requests are answered 'capped' (a paid type is never queued). P2: a new startLead points only at sources or caches of any missing type, and otherwise sends a no-lead; a start never becomes a sighting. PendingSightingType.reason is narrowed to fresh|replacement. Added 6 scripted tests for finding 1 and one start test for the carried-only / late-joiner case. The property checker now allows one sighting message per player per step and checks every free trigger (a loss or a stale rumor) that needs a sighting: it must be in that step's message or in the pending set, and may wait only if the player was capped or the older snapshot can't answer it. Added property scenario 'quick, alpha, seed 15' so EXERCISED still reaches sighting:several-types. Updated docs/intel.md. Ran npm ci, then npm run typecheck, test:unit (580 passed), test:integration (36 passed) and build: all exit 0. All 10 changed or new scripted tests fail against the old step.ts and pass against the new one.
open_assumptions: Expectations changed in existing tests: 'prefer a sealed source, then a cache, then a carrier sighting' now expects a start no-lead, then a bought (targeted) sighting where it used to expect a deferred start sighting. The 'deferred sightings' describe's spentAtFirstBoundary now spends A's sighting on a bought storm sighting instead of a deferred start one. The assertions of both deferred tests are otherwise unchanged.
A start whose missing types are all carried-only sends a 'no-lead' (reason start), as the 'none' case already did; no starting rumor is given.

A type asked for by both a free trigger and a targeted request in one step goes out once, with reason 'targeted', and the request is answered 'sighting', so it is charged even though the free trigger alone would have delivered it.

Two requests with different ids for the same type in one step before minute 28 are now both 'sighting' (one entry), so both are charged. Before, the second was 'capped'. The task says to answer each targeted request in the message 'sighting'.

A pending type is only merged into the accumulator at a boundary, as the task specifies. Between boundaries it stays pending, and an uncapped message for other types can go out beside it (it could not have been answered then anyway: capped or no snapshot data).

findings.message: Charging semantics widened in step.ts pass 4 (lines 476-484): every targeted request whose type is in the one sighting message is answered 'sighting', so two requests with different ids for the same type in one step both get 'sighting' and both are charged 25 gold for a single sighting entry. This applies before minute 28 (the second used to be 'capped') and after it (the 'lift the sighting cap from the carrier reveal on' test still expects ['sighting','sighting'], but the two requests now share one message and one entry). Also, a request whose type a free trigger in the same step already asks for is charged for a sighting the player would have got for free. The worker disclosed this in open assumptions and docs/intel.md, and it follows the literal task wording. Still, it conflicts with the intel-core intent that gold is charged only for something delivered. The caller (objectives-endgame) should decide whether to answer a second same-type request (or one covered by a free trigger) as not charged.
findings.requirement: answer each targeted request in it `sighting`

findings.message: A pending type joins the accumulator only on a step that crosses a snapshot boundary (step.ts:406-409 and 480). With the default rules this is harmless: between boundaries a pending type is either capped or has no snapshot data. But validateIntelRules does not require carrierRevealTicks to be a multiple of carrierIntervalTicks. With a misaligned reveal, a type capped before minute 28 stays pending past the reveal, and a new loss in that gap goes out in its own uncapped message, so the two reach the player in separate messages up to one interval apart. Either require the alignment in the validator or merge the pending set into the accumulator whenever the player is uncapped.
findings.requirement: It starts with the player's pending set if a boundary was crossed.

findings.message: No test checks that a sighting message's type order and sector choice are independent of the order in which triggers joined the accumulator. In every multi-type scripted case in packages/simulation/src/intel/intel.test.ts (lines 447-605: the pending sun+moon pair, pending sun/moon/tide, two losses, a sun loss plus a storm replacement, a sun loss plus a storm request, a batched sun+moon, and a pending sun plus a moon loss on the boundary tick), triggers join in an order that already matches type order (sun, moon, tide, storm). Each of those types also has exactly one sector option, so no sector draw is ever contested. The property Checker (property.test.ts:425-455) never checks the order of the sightings or the sector choice against trigger order. Two regressions would therefore pass the whole suite: dropping the `.sort(byTypeOrder)` at step.ts:468 (the message would then follow Map insertion order), or drawing each sector when its trigger is added. A missing test would need triggers that arrive out of type order, for example a moon loss plus a sun replacement, or a pending storm plus a sun loss on a boundary, with at least two sectors per type. It would then compare against the same step with the triggers in the opposite order.
findings.requirement: The message's type order and sector choice must not depend on the order in which triggers were added.

findings.message: The property Checker records each sighting's reason without checking it. property.test.ts:438 only does EXERCISED.add(`sighting:${sighting.reason}`), and CarrierSighting.reason is typed IntelLeadReason, which includes "start" (state.ts:295). So the eight seeded runs, which include late joiners and carried-only worlds, would still pass if a start produced a carrier sighting. Only two scripted worlds prove that a start never sights (intel.test.ts:150-169 and 199-201). The checker should reject any sighting whose reason is not fresh, targeted or replacement.
findings.requirement: A start never produces a carrier sighting, as `features/intel-core/intel-task.md` specifies (sightings only on a fresh loss, a targeted rumor, or a journal replacement).

# Decisions: intel-core-fixes-2

From the overnight session of 2026-09-24/25. The operator is asleep and asked the assistant to decide, record each decision, and use the workflow for the code.

## Decisions

- intel-core-fixes-001 passed every check. Its general reviewer blocked it on the same late-sighting symptom through another path: triggers on one tick were still handled one type at a time. This follow-up restores that run's snapshot (`2309421`) on its base (`7c82a04`), so the whole feature is reviewed again.
- One sighting accumulator per player per step, joined by losses, replacements and targeted requests, with one emit decision at the end of the step (the challenge's alternative). Targeted requests are answered `sighting` or `capped` by that decision, and a capped paid type is never queued. "Learns about both at once" then holds on every path, including batched ticks and the boundary tick.
- Starting rumors never become carrier sightings: the starting rumor goes to another missing type with a source or cache target, and only when none has one is there no starting rumor. Sightings stay on the three triggers the spec names.

## Assumptions

- Everything else in the earlier intel decisions stands.

## Deferred

- Wiring and the journal UI: `objectives-endgame`.

concerns.message: The plan's delivery rule leaves no room for a free trigger that has nothing left to deliver. The property checker says "every free trigger is delivered in that step's message or the next boundary's", with no exception. But the emit only lists "still-eligible types from the older snapshot", and a type can drop out: the player gets the type back, or the older snapshot has no usable carrier entry. A common case is a fresh theft: in the older snapshot the victim still held the stolen copy, and the victim's own entries are excluded, while the other copies may have been sealed 30–60 s ago. intel-core-fixes had the exception "or dropped only because its type became ineligible, which the checker verifies". This plan doesn't repeat it.
concerns.consequence: A checker written as stated fails on ordinary property seeds. The worker then weakens it on the fly or drops the trigger silently. Either way a victim of a theft can get no lead at all, against §11's "give them a free fresh rumor", and the reviewers could block a third time.

concerns.message: The accumulator "starts with the player's pending set if a boundary was crossed", and when capped it "keeps the free types as the single pending set". Read literally, a capped step with no boundary builds an accumulator without the existing pending types and then replaces pending with only this step's free types. The same condition misfires at minute 28 when minute 28 isn't on a carrier boundary. That happens with compressed property-test configs; the real constants line up, since 1680 s is 56 × 30 s. There the cap lifts, a new trigger emits a message, and the older pending types still wait for the next boundary.
concerns.consequence: Earlier deferred types are overwritten and lost, or a pending type arrives in a second message. That breaks "learns about both at once", the rule this run exists to enforce, and the reviewers may find the same symptom again.

concerns.message: The plan doesn't say when a targeted request's eligibility is judged against the older snapshot. If it is judged when the request joins the accumulator, and on a boundary tick that happens before the snapshots rotate, the request can be answered `sighting` while the emitted message holds no entry for its type. The only outcomes the decision can give are `sighting` or `capped`, so it has no `none` for a type that has become ineligible.
concerns.consequence: The caller charges 25 gold for a sighting that was never delivered, which breaks intel-core's rule that gold is charged only when something is delivered (§11).

concerns.message: The rule that type order and sector choice must not depend on trigger order means generator draws must move to the single emit point, in sorted type order. Moving them changes how the seeded generator is used compared with the snapshot. Scripted tests that assert specific seeded sectors or rumor targets may change even when their scenario has nothing to do with batching.
concerns.consequence: Existing tests fail for reasons that have nothing to do with the findings. The worker must either change expectations, which the task allows only when reported, or keep draws per type and risk depending on trigger order. This uses up the new sixty-minute budget.

concerns.message: Finding 2's case, where every copy of a missing type is carried at the start, can't happen in real matches. At control start all 12 copies are sealed, and §2 bars late arrivals. So the new fallback, which moves the starting rumor to another missing type, is exercised only by the scripted test.
concerns.consequence: This is low risk. But if the start trigger can fire for a player who first appears after control start, for example on reconnect, the fallback changes generator use and replay hashes for those runs. Say which trigger counts as "start" in `docs/intel.md`.

challenge.simpler_alternative: Drop the \"if a boundary was crossed\" condition and use one rule for every player in every step. The accumulator is the pending set plus this step's triggers: losses, replacements and targeted sighting requests, each judged after the snapshots rotate. Emitting is allowed when the tick is at or past minute 28, or when no sighting has been sent for the current snapshot. If allowed, check eligibility once against the older snapshot, in sorted type order. Emit one message if any type is eligible and clear pending. Answer each targeted request `sighting` if its type is in the message and `none` otherwise. A type with nothing to deliver, or no message at all, uses up no cap. If not allowed, pending becomes the free part of the accumulator, which is a union because pending is in it, and targeted requests are answered `capped`. There is then one code path with no special case for boundaries or minute 28. The checker's exception becomes \"delivered, or ineligible at the emit that should have carried it\", and the checker can recompute that directly.
challenge.cheap_experiment: After restoring the snapshot, and before changing `step.ts`, add only the instrumentation to the existing seeded property runs. For each free trigger, record whether its type has any usable entry (one not held by the victim) in the older snapshot at the emit that should carry it. Also count steps with more than one sighting message per player. If free triggers with no usable entry are common, especially right after a theft, decide first whether they are dropped (and the checker exempts them) or kept pending until an entry appears. Also decide whether a targeted request in that state is answered `none`. Record those choices in `docs/intel.md` before rewriting the accumulator. The counts take minutes to get and settle the one rule the plan leaves open.

# Task: intel

## Goal

Deliver `intel-core` (the pure rumors, journal, sectors and reveals) with its remaining review findings fixed. Run intel-core-fixes-001 fixed the first deferred-sighting bug and passed every check, but its general reviewer found the same symptom on another path. Sightings triggered on one tick are still handled one type at a time, so the second type waits up to a whole interval. Start from that run's snapshot, fix it for good, and the whole feature is reviewed again.

## Context

- `features/intel-core/intel-task.md` and `decisions.md`, and `features/intel-core-fixes/intel-task.md` and `decisions.md`, define the feature, and all of it still applies. Read them first.
- **First step:** restore intel-core-fixes-001's snapshot (commit `2309421`) into your worktree, deletions included, but not `features/`:
  `git restore --source=refs/workflow/57859d023c4770f7/intel --staged --worktree -- . ':!features'`.
  Check with `git diff --stat refs/workflow/57859d023c4770f7/intel -- . ':!features'` (it must print nothing). Then read `docs/intel.md` and `packages/simulation/src/intel/step.ts` (`freeLead`, `flushPending`, lines 380–440).
- The verifier runs `npm ci`, then `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test:unit`, `npm run test:integration` and `npm run build`.
- Other features run at the same time and own other paths. Stay inside your owned paths.
- **This machine is shared by several runs. Never stop processes by name pattern (`pkill -f`, `killall`, and so on). Stop only the PIDs you started.**

## Findings to fix (general reviewer)

1. **(P1) One sighting decision per player per step.** Today `freeLead` runs once per type (`step.ts:417` for losses, `:434` for replacements), and the first uncapped call flushes a one-type message and uses up the snapshot's sighting.
   - **Fix: one accumulator, one emit point.** Each player gets one sighting accumulator per step, a sorted set of types.
     - It starts with the player's pending set if a boundary was crossed.
     - Losses, journal replacements **and targeted requests** all add their type to it. None of them flushes on its own.
     - After every pass of the step, each player gets exactly one decision. If the cap allows (or it's minute 28 or later), emit **one** message listing every still-eligible type from the older snapshot, and answer each targeted request in it `sighting`. Otherwise keep the **free** types as the single pending set, and answer targeted requests `capped`. A capped paid type is never queued, so a purchase is never charged for something deferred.
     - The message's type order and sector choice must not depend on the order in which triggers were added.
   - **Scripted tests:**
     - two uncapped losses on one tick give one message with both types;
     - a loss plus a replacement on one tick give one message;
     - a loss plus a targeted request on one tick give one message, and the request is `sighting`;
     - a capped tick with a loss and a targeted request leaves the loss pending and the request `capped`;
     - two losses in one batched view (skipped ticks) give one message;
     - a trigger on the boundary tick itself is included in that boundary's message.
   - **Property checker:** at most one sighting message per player per step. Every free trigger is delivered in that step's message or the next boundary's. Fix `docs/intel.md` wherever it describes this.
2. **(P2) No carrier sighting on the start trigger.** A starting rumor (§2) targets only sealed sources or caches. If every copy of a missing type is carried at the start (for example a late joiner), the starting rumor goes to another missing type that has a source or cache target (§2's "a rumor leading toward a reachable objective"). Only when no missing type has one is there no starting rumor (documented). A start never produces a carrier sighting, as `features/intel-core/intel-task.md` specifies (sightings only on a fresh loss, a targeted rumor, or a journal replacement). Update the scripted test that asserts the old behaviour, and add `start`'s carried-only case to the tests. `EXERCISED` stays with the three sighting triggers.

## Constraints

- Owned paths as in `policy.json`. Apart from restoring the snapshot, change only what the findings need. Keep the structure, names and every existing test, except where this task changes an expectation (say which in your report).

## Acceptance

- The restored feature meets `features/intel-core/intel-task.md` and `features/intel-core-fixes/intel-task.md`.
- Findings 1–2 are fixed with the tests they name.
- `npm ci` then `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test:unit`, `npm run test:integration` and `npm run build` pass from a clean checkout.

## Stop

Report `blocked` instead of continuing when any of these happens:

- Restoring the snapshot fails or touches a path outside the owned paths.
- `npm ci` or an install fails twice for reasons outside the repository (registry, network).
- A check can pass only by changing a path outside the owned paths.
- After sixty minutes of work, any required check still fails and you cannot name the next fix.

Report `question` only for a choice that would change this acceptance.

completion.summary: Restored intel-core-fixes-001's snapshot (2309421), which changed nothing outside the owned paths. P1: step.ts replaces defer/flushPending with one sighting accumulator per player per step. The pending types (at a boundary), losses, journal replacements and targeted requests all add to it, and a new pass 4 makes one decision per player: uncapped, one message lists the types in type order with sectors drawn at send time, and requests are answered 'sighting'; capped, the free types become the one pending set and requests are answered 'capped' (a paid type is never queued). P2: a new startLead points only at sources or caches of any missing type, and otherwise sends a no-lead; a start never becomes a sighting. PendingSightingType.reason is narrowed to fresh|replacement. Added 6 scripted tests for finding 1 and one start test for the carried-only / late-joiner case. The property checker now allows one sighting message per player per step and checks every free trigger (a loss or a stale rumor) that needs a sighting: it must be in that step's message or in the pending set, and may wait only if the player was capped or the older snapshot can't answer it. Added property scenario 'quick, alpha, seed 15' so EXERCISED still reaches sighting:several-types. Updated docs/intel.md. Ran npm ci, then npm run typecheck, test:unit (580 passed), test:integration (36 passed) and build: all exit 0. All 10 changed or new scripted tests fail against the old step.ts and pass against the new one.
open_assumptions: Expectations changed in existing tests: 'prefer a sealed source, then a cache, then a carrier sighting' now expects a start no-lead, then a bought (targeted) sighting where it used to expect a deferred start sighting. The 'deferred sightings' describe's spentAtFirstBoundary now spends A's sighting on a bought storm sighting instead of a deferred start one. The assertions of both deferred tests are otherwise unchanged.
A start whose missing types are all carried-only sends a 'no-lead' (reason start), as the 'none' case already did; no starting rumor is given.

A type asked for by both a free trigger and a targeted request in one step goes out once, with reason 'targeted', and the request is answered 'sighting', so it is charged even though the free trigger alone would have delivered it.

Two requests with different ids for the same type in one step before minute 28 are now both 'sighting' (one entry), so both are charged. Before, the second was 'capped'. The task says to answer each targeted request in the message 'sighting'.

A pending type is only merged into the accumulator at a boundary, as the task specifies. Between boundaries it stays pending, and an uncapped message for other types can go out beside it (it could not have been answered then anyway: capped or no snapshot data).
untested: The random property runs never produce two sighting triggers for one player on the same step, so the new per-step property checks pass against the old step.ts too. Only the scripted tests catch the bug.
Two targeted requests with different ids for the same type in one step before minute 28 (charging both).
A carrier reveal tick that is not on a carrier boundary (a config where the interval does not divide minute 28).
completion.verify_yourself: That charging a targeted request which shares its type with a free trigger in the same step (or with a second request for the same type) is acceptable. The code answers every such request 'sighting', so the caller charges 25 gold for each.
